question.text: Will Nueva Pescanova's octopus farm gain regulatory approval in the Canary Islands before June 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before June 1, 2027, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) report that Nueva Pescanova has been officially granted regulatory approval by [the Government of the Canary Islands](https://www.gobiernodecanarias.org/principal/) to operate an octopus farm in the Canary Islands.
question.fine_print:
To qualify, the regulatory approval must be for a facility operated by Nueva Pescanova with the purpose of the production, processing, and distribution of octopuses for human consumption.

The farm does not need to be operational for this question to resolve as Yes.

research:
The question looks almost settled. Nueva Pescanova formally withdrew its application for the Las Palmas octopus farm in July 2026, and the file is being archived. That makes a Canary Islands government approval before June 1, 2027 very unlikely unless a new application is filed.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question has no data series. It resolves on credible reports that the Government of the Canary Islands granted approval. I did not fetch the government homepage, which is not a status tracker. I found no report of any approval, at any time.
- 2026-01: the procedure for the discharge permit (autorización de vertidos) was declared lapsed. [ecoticias](https://www.ecoticias.com/naturaleza/nueva-pescanova-renuncia-a-la-granja-de-pulpos-en-canarias)
- 2026-05: the Las Palmas Port Authority started proceedings to lapse the concession file, which had been inactive. [ecoticias](https://www.ecoticias.com/naturaleza/nueva-pescanova-renuncia-a-la-granja-de-pulpos-en-canarias), [PACMA](https://pacma.es/notas-de-prensa/pacma-celebra-el-carpetazo-definitivo-al-proyecto-de-granja-de-pulpos-de-nueva-pescanova-en-gran-canaria/)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-07-23: Nueva Pescanova formally told the Las Palmas Port Authority that it was dropping its request for a port concession (a file opened in May 2021). The Authority will archive the file. The company cited "business and regulatory considerations": the regional environmental assessment committee (Comisión Autonómica de Evaluación Ambiental) had imposed new requirements and an ordinary environmental assessment. The company said the project is still technically and environmentally viable. It left the door open if regulations change or "new locations" become available. [Libertad Digital](https://www.libertaddigital.com/canarias/2026-07-23/nueva-pescanova-retira-su-solicitud-para-instalar-una-granja-de-pulpos-en-las-palmas-7439998/), [Press Digital](https://www.pressdigital.es/articulo/economia/2026-07-23/5963402-nueva-pescanova-descarta-granja-pulpos-puerto-palmas-gran-canaria)
- So the background statement that there were "no further updates as of May 2026" is out of date. The project the question is about has been withdrawn.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09: reports say the national bill to ban octopus farming has been published in Congress but has not been passed. [ecoticias](https://www.ecoticias.com/?p=496446)
- 2026-08-05: Infobae and others reported that "the world's first octopus farm will not be in Spain". Coverage says the company's octopus research in Galicia continues. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/espana/2026/08/05/la-primera-granja-de-pulpos-del-mundo-finalmente-no-estara-en-espana-nueva-pescanova-abandona-su-polemico-proyecto-en-gran-canaria/), [Estrella Digital](https://www.estrelladigital.es/articulo/empresas/nueva-pescanova-renuncia-construir-canarias-primera-granja-industrial-pulpos-mundo/20260804211132449546.html), [SeafoodSource](https://www.seafoodsource.com/news/ngos-celebrate-as-nueva-pescanova-ditches-plans-for-octopus-farm) (SeafoodSource blocked access; I saw only the headline)
- 2026-07-24: the animal-rights party PACMA welcomed what it called a "carpetazo definitivo" (final shelving of the project). [PACMA](https://pacma.es/notas-de-prensa/pacma-celebra-el-carpetazo-definitivo-al-proyecto-de-granja-de-pulpos-de-nueva-pescanova-en-gran-canaria/)
- 2026-05-08: El Español reported growing pressure in Congress to stop intensive octopus aquaculture. [El Español](https://www.elespanol.com/ciencia/20260508/espana-endurece-limites-pulpo-fija-ley-peso-minimo-venta-busca-vetar-cria-intensiva-granjas/1003744232604_0.html)
- I found no news from September to November 2026 of a new site or a new filing in the Canary Islands. None of the news-API articles supplied are relevant (they cover bullying, electricity, budgets and so on).

## 4. Base rates
- Since 2021 the project has gone backwards: the 2023 environmental report was judged insufficient, permits lapsed in 2026, and the application was withdrawn in July 2026. It never obtained approval at any stage in about 5 years.
- Approval would require a brand-new application and a full ordinary environmental impact assessment. In Spain that process usually takes years, not about 7 months. Given that, I found no precedent for approval within the remaining window.
- No commercial octopus farm has been approved anywhere in the EU as far as I could find. Bans have been passed or proposed elsewhere: California passed one in 2024, and Chile and Mexico have bills.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the markets supplied matches this question: they cover a US farm bill, FDA decisions and a US Supreme Court case.
- The Kalshi market on the 2027 Canary Islands election is only loosely relevant, as a signal of the future regional government: PSOE 0.55, CC 0.33, PP 0.10.
- I found no Polymarket, Manifold or expert forecast on this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Nueva Pescanova could announce an alternative site or project, possibly in the Canary Islands. It has said this is possible but has announced nothing concrete.
- The national bill banning octopus aquaculture (filed by Sumar and partners in June 2025, BOCG 15-B-241-1) is still pending; no plenary vote date found. [Congreso](https://www.congreso.es/public_oficiales/L15/CONG/BOCG/B/BOCG-15-B-241-1.PDF)
- Canary Islands regional elections are due around May 2027. A change of government could alter the regulatory climate, but not in time for an approval before June 1, 2027.

**Bottom line:** Nueva Pescanova formally dropped its Gran Canaria octopus farm in July 2026, before any approval was granted. As of November 5, 2026, I could not find any new Canary Islands application. That leaves almost no time for a fresh approval before June 1, 2027.

### 1. Resolution source
- No set data series decides this one. It resolves on credible reports that the Government of the Canary Islands has granted approval. I did not fetch the government's homepage (gobiernodecanarias.org). I found no report anywhere of an approval, then or now.
- 2021-05: the application was filed with the Las Palmas Port Authority, which handles the port land concession. The regional government ran the environmental assessment. [LD Canarias](https://www.libertaddigital.com/canarias/2026-07-23/nueva-pescanova-retira-su-solicitud-para-instalar-una-granja-de-pulpos-en-las-palmas-7439998/)

### 2. Current status: very close to settled as No
- 2026-07-23: Nueva Pescanova formally told the Port Authority of Las Palmas it was withdrawing its concession application for the farm. The Port Authority is to archive the file opened in 2021. The company said tougher regulatory requirements and delays made the investment unviable "under current conditions". It said the project is still technically and environmentally feasible, and that it may look at alternatives "if the regulatory context changes or new location options arise". [LD Canarias](https://www.libertaddigital.com/canarias/2026-07-23/nueva-pescanova-retira-su-solicitud-para-instalar-una-granja-de-pulpos-en-las-palmas-7439998/); [PressDigital](https://www.pressdigital.es/articulo/economia/2026-07-23/5963402-nueva-pescanova-descarta-granja-pulpos-puerto-palmas-gran-canaria)

[WeAreAquaculture](https://weareaquaculture.com/news/aquaculture/nueva-pescanova-withdraws-plans-for-the-worlds-first-octopus-farm); [FoodIngredientsFirst](https://www.foodingredientsfirst.com/news/nueva-pescanova-abandons-octopus-farm.html)
- Since then I found no reports of a new site or application in the Canary Islands, through early November 2026.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-05: Infobae says the "first octopus farm in the world will not be in Spain". esdiario says the €65M, 300-job project "flees Spain" under pressure from Sumar, ERC and Podemos. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/espana/2026/08/05/la-primera-granja-de-pulpos-del-mundo-finalmente-no-estara-en-espana-nueva-pescanova-abandona-su-polemico-proyecto-en-gran-canaria/); [esdiario](https://www.esdiario.com/nacional/260805/194842/granja-pulpos-70-millones-300-empleos-huye-espana-cercada-sumar-erc.html)
- 2026-08-04: Estrella Digital reports the company giving up on the Canary Islands farm. [Estrella Digital](https://www.estrelladigital.es/articulo/empresas/nueva-pescanova-renuncia-construir-canarias-primera-granja-industrial-pulpos-mundo/20260804211132449546.html)
- 2026-07-24: the animal rights party PACMA welcomes the "definitive" end of the project. It describes this as the company withdrawing, not as a government rejection. [PACMA](https://pacma.es/notas-de-prensa/pacma-celebra-el-carpetazo-definitivo-al-proyecto-de-granja-de-pulpos-de-nueva-pescanova-en-gran-canaria/)
- 2026-05: according to search summaries of press reports, the Port Authority started proceedings to declare the project file lapsed because it had been inactive for years. I did not verify this in a primary source.
- 2026-01: according to the same unverified search summaries, the procedure for the farm's wastewater discharge permit was declared lapsed. [Ecoticias](https://www.ecoticias.com/naturaleza/nueva-pescanova-renuncia-a-la-granja-de-pulpos-en-canarias)
- Earlier: the regional government found the environmental report insufficient and ordered a full ("ordinary") environmental assessment because of possible significant negative effects. [elDiario.es](https://www.eldiario.es/canariasahora/ciencia_y_medio_ambiente/granja-pulpos-canarias-continua-evaluacion-ambiental-hallarse-posibles-efectos-adversos-significativos_1_11323860.html)

### 4. Base rates
- This project spent about 5 years (2021 to 2026) in permitting without getting approval. It never got past the environmental assessment.
- A new Canary Islands project would need a new concession application, an environmental impact assessment and a discharge permit. On this project's record, each of those took years. Getting all of them done within about 7 months would be very unusual.
- I know of no commercial octopus farm that has been approved anywhere. Some US states, including Washington and California, have banned octopus farming.

### 5. Other forecasts
- None of the supplied markets matches this question. They cover the US farm bill, FDA decisions and SCOTUS.
- One is loosely relevant: Kalshi's 2027 Canary Islands regional election market (PSOE 0.55, CC 0.33, PP 0.10). The election is expected in May 2027, but this market says nothing directly about octopus farm approval.
- I found no Polymarket or Manifold market and no expert forecast on this question.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The Port Authority formally archiving the file. That is procedural and would confirm the end of the project.
- Any Nueva Pescanova announcement of a new site or technical redesign. The company has left this possibility open, but has given no timeline or location. Its octopus research continues in Galicia.
- The Canary Islands regional elections, expected in May 2027, could change the regulatory climate, but any change would come after the question closes.
- National legislative moves against octopus farming, for example proposals from Sumar or ERC.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 7 months remain until the June 1, 2027 deadline, with resolution around July 2027. For Yes, credible sources must report that the Government of the Canary Islands officially granted Nueva Pescanova regulatory approval to operate an octopus farm for human consumption in the islands.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. On 2026-07-23 Nueva Pescanova formally withdrew its port concession application in Las Palmas. The discharge permit procedure had already lapsed in January 2026, and the file is being archived. No application is now pending.

(c) Base rate: the reference class is withdrawn or lapsed controversial aquaculture or industrial projects in Spain that were refiled and approved within about a year. That rate is near 0%, well under 2%. A new filing would need an ordinary environmental impact assessment, which typically takes years. No commercial octopus farm has been approved anywhere in the EU.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes (weak): the company said in July 2026 that the project remains technically viable and left the door open to "new locations" or regulatory changes. Its octopus research in Galicia continues.
- For No (strong):
  - The application was formally withdrawn on 2026-07-23.
  - The permits lapsed in January and May 2026.
  - The 2023 environmental report was judged insufficient.
  - The regional commission required an ordinary environmental assessment.
  - A national bill to ban octopus farming is pending in Congress.
  - There was no news of any new filing through November 2026.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: the file stays archived, the company focuses on research or sites outside Spain, the regional elections come in May 2027, and no approval is granted. This is the overwhelmingly likely path.
- Yes: the company quietly refiles at a new Canary site in late 2026 with an already complete environmental study, and the regional government fast-tracks it before June 2027. This is very implausible given the timelines and the political climate.

(f) I start from a base rate near 0 to 1%. The withdrawal effectively decides the outcome, because approval would require a new application plus a multi-year assessment completed within 7 months. I keep a small residual for resolution quirks, such as a misreported approval of some component, or an unknown pending filing. No matching market exists.

Probability: 1%
